lessons.title: Present simple: am, is, are
lessons.summary: Say who or what someone is.
rule: Use is with he, she and it.
Use are with we, you and they.

questions.why: With he, she and it we use is.
With we, you and they we use are.
With I we use am.
He takes is, so "He is tall." is correct.
With we we use are.

lessons.title: Present simple: daily routines
lessons.summary: Talk about things you do regularly.
rule: Use the base verb with I, you, we and they.
With he, she and it the verb usually takes -s or -es.
If a verb ends in consonant + y, change y to -ies (study becomes studies).

examples.text: He goes to school every morning.

questions.why: With he the verb takes -es: goes.
With they we use the base verb: play.
Consonant + y changes to -ies: studies.
Verbs ending in -ch add -es: watches.
With I we use the base verb: eat.

lessons.title: Present simple: questions and negatives
lessons.summary: Ask questions and say what is not true.
rule: Use do/does to make questions: Do you like tea? Does she work here?
Use do not (don't) or does not (doesn't) to make negatives.
After do/does the main verb stays in its base form: She doesn't like coffee.

questions.why: With you we use Do.
With she we use does not.
With he we use Does.
After doesn't the verb stays in the base form: eat.
With they we use do not.

lessons.title: Articles: a, an, the
lessons.summary: Choose the right small word before a noun.
rule: Use a before a consonant sound and an before a vowel sound.
Use the when we already know which one, or when there is only one.
It is the sound that matters: an honest man (the h is silent).

questions.why: Apple starts with a vowel sound, so we use an.
Teacher starts with a consonant sound, so we use a.

questions.prompt: I bought a book. ___ book is interesting.
questions.why: We already mentioned the book, so we use the.
Honest starts with a vowel sound because the h is silent, so we use an.
There is only one sun, so we use the.

lessons.title: Plural nouns
lessons.summary: Make nouns plural, including irregular ones.
rule: Most nouns add -s: book becomes books.
Nouns ending in -s, -x, -ch or -sh add -es: box becomes boxes.
Consonant + y changes to -ies: baby becomes babies.
Some nouns are irregular: child becomes children, man becomes men.

questions.why: Nouns ending in -x add -es.
Child has an irregular plural: children.
Consonant + y changes to -ies.
Nouns ending in -s add -es.
Man has an irregular plural: men.
